import sys, json, hashlib, datetime

# The fast lane. Four recipes, rendered from parameters that `classify` has
# already validated. No model, no network, no disk: what leaves here is a string
# built out of a dict.

# --8<-- digest-helper
def canonical(declarations):
    # Canonical bytes: keys sorted, no spaces, no ascii escaping. The digest has
    # to survive a round trip through a CHAT -- the draft is shown to a human,
    # the model repeats it in the second tool call, and the submitter refuses
    # anything whose bytes changed on the way. Without that, the manifest a
    # human said yes to and the manifest that gets applied are only PROBABLY
    # the same one.
    return json.dumps(declarations, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"),
                      ensure_ascii=False)


def digest(declarations):
    return hashlib.sha256(canonical(declarations).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
# --8<-- end

# GH #480 -- the same six coordinates `templates/builder/weave` writes down when
# a composer opens a round. They are named here because the FAST LANE opens no
# round: there is no model call behind a recipe, so nothing on this lane ever
# reached the round table, and a refusal that came back for a model-free build
# found no owner for its digest and no door to answer to.
CALLER_KEYS = ("build_call_id", "agent", "build_op", "build_scope",
               "build_caller", "build_auto_submit")


def rewire_edge(p):
    edge = {"from": p["from"], "to": p["to"]}
    if p.get("condition"):
        edge["condition"] = p["condition"]
    # Remove FIRST. A manifest rolls forward and stops at the first refusal,
    # with no rollback (R5): an add that lands before its remove leaves both
    # edges live if the remove is then refused, which is a silent fan-out, not
    # a rewire.
    return [
        {"scope": p["scope"], "ctx": {},
         "diff": {"remove_edges": [{"match": {"from": p["from"], "to": p["old_to"]}}]}},
        {"scope": p["scope"], "ctx": {}, "diff": {"add_edges": [edge]}},
    ]


def add_node(p):
    # `add_timer` was the third recipe in the plan; the tree ships no standalone
    # timer template, and inventing one to make a recipe true would be the tail
    # wagging the dog. The class it stood for -- grow a cell and wire it in --
    # survives with the template as a PARAMETER, which makes the recipe useful
    # for every single-cell template instead of exactly one.
    node = {"name": p["name"], "template": p["template"]}
    if isinstance(p.get("override_params"), dict):
        node["override_params"] = p["override_params"]
    return [
        {"scope": p["scope"], "ctx": {}, "diff": {"add_nodes": [node]}},
        {"scope": p["scope"], "ctx": {},
         "diff": {"add_edges": [{"from": "./" + p["name"], "to": p["target"],
                                 "modifier": {"set_hop": {"route": "'%s'" % p["route"]}}}]}},
    ]


def attach_drain(p):
    return [{"scope": p["scope"], "ctx": {},
             "diff": {"add_edges": [{"from": p["from"], "to": p["to"],
                 "condition": "has(hop.route) && hop.route == '%s'" % p["route"]}]}}]



# --- the round a channel speaks in (GH #517) --------------------------------
#
# A round is PROVENANCE, and provenance is not derived. Until this repair the
# channel level read the member's identity off the DIRECTORY NAME of the scope
# the wish had named -- `.../members/egon` became `member:egon` -- which is the
# right answer only while the folder happens to be spelled like the person.
# Where it was not, the ingress edge declared a round that exists in no row of
# the store, and the audience gate (`memory-hive/recall`, `visible()`,
# `audience_now` subset of `row_audience`) refused every single one of them:
# 34 facts, 182 episodes, four legs, ZERO candidates, and a bundle saying
# "Nothing in this memory answers this question" -- the same sentence a
# genuinely empty store produces. Silent, total, and indistinguishable from
# having no memory at all (measured on a live colony, GH #517).
#
# So the person is a thing the WISH says. It travels in the declaration's own
# `ctx` block under `member_person`, and a wish that does not say it is ASKED
# rather than guessed at. `ctx` is where it lives for a second reason: the
# claim then stands in the rendered manifest, in front of the reviewer, before
# it is committed -- and the mutation door ignores a ctx key no template of the
# declaration requires (`validate::check_declared_requirements` reads the
# template's REQUIRED keys and nothing else).
#
# `templates/receptionist/greet` already writes the rule this recipe broke: a
# door that was told no audience leaves it EMPTY -- "a channel identity is a
# room, not a participant, and turning one into the other would invent a member
# nobody named". A recipe cannot leave it empty, because an empty round is
# refused by the holders; so it asks.
#
# THE OTHER HALF IS NOT THE SAME DEFECT. `agent:<assistant>` is built from
# `p["assistant"]`, which is a PARAMETER OF THE WISH -- "the agent this
# channel's turns default to" -- and not a string carved out of a path. It is
# the one name the wish is already required to say (LEVEL_EXTRA["channel"]), so
# it is a quotation, not a guess. A generation whose affinity identity differs
# from the node it stands in is a case nobody has yet had; when it appears it
# is a second ctx key here, not a derivation.
PERSON_KEY = "member_person"

# The question, verbatim on the wire. A refusal a human cannot read is one they
# cannot answer -- the same rule `normalise` follows when a composer asks for a
# model id instead of inventing one.
PERSON_QUESTION = (
    "who is the PERSON this channel speaks with? A channel's ingress edge "
    "declares the round every turn on it is spoken in -- "
    "[\"agent:<assistant>\", \"member:<person>\"] in affinity vocabulary -- "
    "and that round decides which rows of the member's memory the turn is "
    "allowed to see. It is the person's identity, which is NOT necessarily the "
    "name of the directory the member stands in. Name it as "
    "ctx.%s of the wish." % PERSON_KEY)


class WishIncomplete(Exception):
    """A fact the recipe was not given and will not invent.

    It is not a KeyError, because `recipe_params_incomplete` means "you named a
    recipe and left a parameter out" and this one means "the wish never said".
    They call for opposite repairs: one is a typo in a tool call, the other is a
    question for whoever made the wish.
    """

    def __init__(self, key, question):
        Exception.__init__(self, question)
        self.key = key
        self.question = question


# --- birth ------------------------------------------------------------------
#
# `add_nodes[].birth` (GH #437) decides whether what a declaration places comes
# to the world registered, addressable and TASKLESS or registered and running.
# It is the DOOR's vocabulary and not this recipe's -- `active` (the door's own
# default) or `inactive`, and a third word is refused here rather than carried,
# because the door refuses it too and a manifest that stops halfway through is
# the expensive way to learn about a typo.
BIRTH_STATES = ("active", "inactive")

# The one level whose default is not the door's. A connector opens its upstream
# the moment it has a task -- so a channel grown from a wish is born ASLEEP and
# armed by a second, deliberate act (GH #468), and the wish that wants it awake
# says so and gets `active` written out rather than left to a default. Every
# other level is a composition of cells that wait to be addressed, and waking
# one costs nothing.
LEVEL_BIRTH = {"channel": "inactive"}


# --- grow_level -------------------------------------------------------------
#
# A LEVEL is a recipe, because the edges a new child gets are a property of the
# PARENT and not of the child. `examples/organism` writes them out by hand, once
# per child, and the COUNTS are published exactly once, in the README table of
# this template, with a test deriving them from this renderer. They are not a
# coincidence and not a judgement -- they are the same set every time, with the
# child's name substituted in.
#
# WHY A TABLE AND NOT A DERIVATION. The obvious idea is to compute the set from
# the child's `contract.accepts` / `contract.emits`. It does not work, and the
# reason is worth writing down so nobody re-derives the disappointment:
#
#   * A connector has NO contract at all. `telegram-connector` is a `proxy`
#     cell, its `accepts` and `emits` are both empty, and its two upward edges
#     condition on `has(hop.error_code)` -- on a failure key, not on a lane.
#   * Lane count is not edge count, in both directions. `assistant@2.2.0`
#     declares twenty lanes and gets fourteen edges: `in_advice`, `in_sweep`,
#     `in_prune` and `in_round_sweep` are addressed at the path directly
#     (ruling W7-R5), `in_pack` and `pack_ack` are the opt-in identity door and
#     not part of the level (GH #473), and `display` folds `event`+`receipt`
#     into ONE edge one level further out.
#   * Guards, modifiers and literals live in no contract. `context.assistant ==
#     '<name>'`, the `audience_set` literal, `hop.owner.contains(...)`, the
#     `set_hop.route = 'in_view'` restamp -- addressing is a property of the
#     parent, and `params.contract` has no vocabulary for it.
#
# So: a table, pinned against `examples/organism/grow-*.json` byte for byte by
# `crates/meclaw-cells/tests/gh466_grow_level_renders_the_level.rs`. The example
# and the recipe cannot drift apart, because one is generated from the other's
# table and compared.
#
# WHAT STAYS WITH THE MODEL. The TEMPLATE. This recipe renders edges; it does
# not choose what to grow. Which template a level is filled with is a catalogue
# question, and the catalogue is the librarian's -- the design lane looks it up,
# the fast lane is TOLD it. Same for `ctx`: the recipe passes whatever it was
# given straight into the declaration and asserts nothing about it, because the
# authority on what a template demands is the mutation door, which answers
# `requirement_missing` by name and hands it back on `in_receipt`.


# --- the narrow form, and the scope root a level asks for (GH #503) ----------
#
# A level DECLARES ITSELF AT THE CONTAINER it grows into -- `/os/orgs` for an
# organisation, `<member>/assistants` for an assistant -- and names its child
# bare. Until #503 the declaration stood one storey higher: the scope was the
# container's PARENT and the container travelled inside the node name
# (`orgs/acme`, `./orgs -> ./orgs/acme`). Both forms grow the same tree; the
# absolute edges are identical to the byte. What moves is the declaration's
# SCOPE ROOT, and the scope root is what the broker judges.
#
# That is the whole defect. `templates/access/store/seed/policy.jsonl` grants
# `colony.mutate.default` under `scope_prefix: "/os/orgs"`, and the FIRST
# organisation of a colony is grown at `/os` -- so the one build every colony
# starts with was refused at the front with `requester_not_permitted`, while
# the very same manifest applied by an operator committed. Every other level
# was already under the prefix and never noticed.
#
# Drawable at all only since GH #487: `.` (and `./`) resolves to the
# declaration's own scope inside `add_edges`, so a container can be addressed
# from the declaration that stands in it. Before that, the wide spelling was
# the only one the door accepted.
#
# ONE FORM FOR EVERY LEVEL, with one measured exception -- the identity door of
# `_assistant_level`, which reaches a hive that is the container's SIBLING and
# is therefore not addressable from inside it at all. See there.


class Place(object):
    """Where a level's declaration stands, and how it spells its child.

    `container` is the hive the child is placed in, and it is the real name in
    both forms: a guard that reads an absolute path (`hop.owner`) names the
    TREE, not the declaration it was written in. `narrow` is whether the
    declaration stands at that hive (the form above) or one storey above it.
    """

    def __init__(self, container, narrow):
        self.container = container
        self.narrow = narrow

    def up(self):
        """The container -- `.` when the declaration already stands in it."""
        return "." if self.narrow else "./" + self.container

    def down(self, name):
        """The child, as an edge endpoint."""
        return ("./" + name) if self.narrow else "./%s/%s" % (self.container, name)

    def node(self, name):
        """The child, as `add_nodes[].name`."""
        return name if self.narrow else "%s/%s" % (self.container, name)

    def scope(self, parent):
        """The declaration's scope, from the scope the WISH named.

        The recipe PARAMETER stays what it always was -- the parent the wish
        talks about ("grow an org under /os"). Only the rendered declaration
        moves down into the container, because that is the address the edges
        are relative to.
        """
        if not self.narrow:
            return parent
        base = str(parent).rstrip("/")
        return "%s/%s" % (base, self.container) if base else "/" + self.container


def _in(place, name, route, guard=""):
    return {"from": place.up(), "to": place.down(name),
            "condition": "has(hop.route) && hop.route == '%s'%s" % (route, guard)}


def _out(place, name, route):
    return {"from": place.down(name), "to": place.up(),
            "condition": "has(hop.route) && hop.route == '%s'" % route}


# The key a container level is ADDRESSED by, one per level. `Edge.to` is a static
# path in this substrate, so two children of one container cost two edges and
# each one has to say WHICH child it is for -- the address rule of this
# template's README, read one storey above the assistant it was written for.
# Until GH #478 the six doors below carried the lane and nothing else, which is
# an address only while a container holds exactly one child; with two, every
# message on the lane is delivered TWICE.
CONTAINER_KEY = {"orgs": "org", "members": "member"}


def _container_level(place, name, _p):
    # org and member are the SAME shape one level apart, and that is a claim
    # about their two contracts rather than a convenience: org@1.3.0 and
    # member@1.4.0 declare the same seven accepts and the same eleven emits,
    # and each one's parent already carries every one of those lanes into the
    # container its child is grown into. Six doors down, eleven exits back up.
    #
    # `in_import` is the seventh accept and gets NO edge, which is the rule
    # above read once more: an import addresses the level's OWN path, so an
    # edge from the container could never deliver one -- and a member already
    # running is the only thing it is for (`examples/memory-import/`, edges()).
    #
    # The ORDER is the one `build_import.py` writes. That tool is the second
    # generator of this very set, and the two are compared element for element
    # by `gh470_a_grown_container_level_carries_its_export_lanes.rs` -- so the
    # order is not a style choice here either, it is what makes the comparison
    # a comparison. This table stood at thirteen edges from before the member
    # had a memory export (GH #470); nothing was red, because the byte pin
    # compared it against examples generated from itself.
    #
    # The discriminator is PERMISSIVE and not strict (GH #478). Nothing in a
    # grown topology promotes `context.member` or `context.org` today, so
    # `has(...) && ... == name` would strand every existing colony's turns at
    # the container the day it landed. Without the key the fan-out is what it
    # always was; with it, the turn reaches exactly one child. It is the form
    # `_assistant_level` already writes for `in_build_result`, and the one
    # `templates/meclaw-os/config.json` uses for `context.build_caller`.
    key = CONTAINER_KEY[place.container]
    guard = " && (!has(context.%s) || context.%s == '%s')" % (key, key, name)
    edges = [_in(place, name, r, guard)
             for r in ("in_turn", "in_recall", "in_brief", "in_propose",
                       "in_build_result", "in_export")]
    edges += [_out(place, name, r)
              for r in ("answer", "bundle", "ack", "reject", "error", "write",
                        "turn_write", "prune", "build", "close_report",
                        "export_done", "pack_ack")]
    return edges


def _assistant_level(place, name, p):
    # The address rule, v1 (GH #454): ONE edge per assistant, guarded on
    # `context.assistant`, because `Edge.to` is a static path in this substrate.
    # There is no edge meaning "send it wherever the context says", and there
    # will not be one -- so N assistants cost N edges and never N x M.
    guard = " && has(context.assistant) && context.assistant == '%s'" % name
    edges = [_in(place, name, "in_turn", guard),
             _in(place, name, "in_bundle", guard)]
    edges += [_out(place, name, r)
              for r in ("answer", "recall", "extraction", "write",
                        "turn_write", "prune", "error")]
    build = _out(place, name, "build")
    build["modifier"] = {"set_context": {"assistant": "'%s'" % name}}
    edges.append(build)
    # A build result with NO assistant on the context belongs to whoever asked;
    # one that names an assistant belongs to that one alone.
    edges.append(_in(place, name, "in_build_result",
                     " && (!has(context.assistant) || context.assistant == '%s')" % name))
    # GH #476 -- the transfer lanes GH #475 opened. A generation holds ONE store
    # its member cannot recompute: the session ledger four levels down in its
    # own `session-keeper`, which decides whether a conversation continues or
    # starts at zero. `in_export` and `in_import` are addressed with the SAME
    # key a turn is, because a member with two generations has two ledgers and
    # they are not one document -- and the sink files a part under the hive it
    # came out of, so two keepers would write one directory.
    #
    # The way back is a PLAIN `dump`. Every level between this container and the
    # keeper pairs `in_export` with `dump` in `params.required_drains`, and the
    # probe that checks the pairing runs the described hop through the real edge
    # evaluator -- an edge that additionally tested `hop.dump_kind` evaluates
    # false under it and reads as no drain at all, so the mutation is refused.
    edges.append(_in(place, name, "in_export", guard))
    edges.append(_in(place, name, "in_import", guard))
    edges.append(_out(place, name, "dump"))
    # GH #473 -- the identity door, and it is OPT-IN rather than part of the
    # level. A grown assistant reaches its brain with an EMPTY `system` tree:
    # nothing in a grown topology writes a durable slot, and the one lane that
    # can (`in_pack`, GH #458) has to be drawn from the member's own record.
    #
    # Two edges, the shape `templates/affinity/README.md` publishes: the push
    # leaves the affinity HIVE on `answer` and is told apart from the tool lane
    # by `hop.subscriber`, restamped onto the subscriber's own `in_pack`; and
    # `in_pack` and `pack_ack` are ONE decision, so the drain is drawn in the
    # same breath or the door refuses both with `required_drain_missing`.
    #
    # WHY OPT-IN. The act has an owner. Since GH #479 the submitter's form
    # check has a second branch for exactly this shape -- a parent may draw an
    # `in_pack` edge into a node the SAME declaration creates -- so a level that
    # always drew one would in fact be submittable. It stays a parameter because
    # writing into a brain's prompt is not something a level does to every
    # generation grown from it without being asked. (Before #479 the rule had one
    # branch, `subscribe_target_not_self` fired on every grown door, and the
    # opt-in had no reachable caller at all.) The ROW is
    # the other half and is not renderable at all: a `subscribers` row is a
    # store write, and writing it stays a `subscribe` op through affinity's own
    # gate (ruling R-Subscribe). What this renders is the half a manifest can
    # carry -- the graph the row will need.
    #
    # WHY THIS ONE LEVEL KEEPS THE WIDE FORM (GH #503, and it is measured).
    # `./affinity` is a SIBLING of `./assistants`, one storey up. From a
    # declaration standing IN the container the only spellings that could reach
    # it are `../affinity` and an absolute path, and `mutation::validate` refuses
    # both in an edge endpoint outright (`ScopeOutOfBounds`, and the `..` arm is
    # a security hotfix rather than a lookup miss) -- so in the narrow form the
    # affinity hive is not addressable at all. Splitting the door into a SECOND
    # declaration at the member does not survive either: `templates/submit/gate`
    # accepts an `in_pack` edge only when its target is under the requester or
    # is created by THAT SAME declaration, the requester of a grown door is
    # `/os/operator/submit` (GH #479), and a declaration that only draws edges
    # creates nothing -- measured, it comes back `subscribe_target_not_self`.
    # Widening that check is a change to a security default and wants its own
    # ruling, which is exactly what #503 says option 3 is.
    #
    # The trade is free where it lands: an assistant is grown at
    # `/os/orgs/<org>/members/<member>`, which is under the broker's
    # `/os/orgs` prefix in EITHER form. Nothing reachable becomes unreachable.
    if p.get("subscribe"):
        target = place.down(name)
        edges.append({
            "from": "./affinity", "to": target,
            "condition": "has(hop.route) && hop.route == 'answer' && "
                         "hop.subscriber == '%s'" % target,
            "modifier": {"set_hop": {"route": "'in_pack'"}}})
        edges.append(_out(place, name, "pack_ack"))
    return edges


def _channel_level(place, name, p):
    # A connector raises a turn and stamps WHO it is for. The default agent is a
    # literal on the edge on purpose: a CEL guard is evaluated by the substrate
    # against `hop` and `context` and cannot read a node's `params`, so "the
    # default of this channel" has nowhere else to live.
    #
    # GH #517 -- the round is READ OFF THE WISH and never off the scope. See
    # PERSON_KEY above for the failure the old derivation produced.
    agent = p["assistant"]
    ctx = p.get("ctx") if isinstance(p.get("ctx"), dict) else {}
    person = str(ctx.get(PERSON_KEY) or "").strip()
    if not person:
        raise WishIncomplete(PERSON_KEY, PERSON_QUESTION)
    # GH #517 -- every promotion on this edge is `has(...) ? ... : ''`, which is
    # the rule `templates/member/README.md` already publishes for the doors one
    # storey up: a modifier that fails to evaluate SKIPS THE WHOLE EDGE, and a
    # turn that vanishes on an edge is invisible, while a turn that arrives with
    # an empty key is refused by the holder on a lane that is drained, with a
    # reason. The bare `hop.chat_id` this edge used to carry logged
    # `cel eval set_context.chat_id: No such key: chat_id` on every emission the
    # connector makes that is not an inbound message -- its own failures ride
    # the second edge below, and they carry no chat.
    return [
        {"from": place.down(name), "to": place.up(),
         "condition": "!has(hop.error_code)",
         "modifier": {
             "set_hop": {"route": "'turn'"},
             "set_context": {
                 # GH #522 -- TWO keys, because one word was doing two jobs.
                 # `channel_node` is the ADDRESS: the node this turn came out
                 # of, and the word the third edge below routes the answer back
                 # by, because `Edge.to` is static in this substrate and a
                 # container may hold several channels (the address rule, #454).
                 # `channel` is the CHAT: what a surface calls "the same
                 # conversation partner", which is what the session keeper opens
                 # a generation for, what the firewall rate-limits and what a
                 # memory row writes down as the room. Keyed on the node name,
                 # every chat of one connector shared ONE generation, ONE rate
                 # bucket and ONE room -- and the hand-drawn e9-era edge, whose
                 # rows are the history that actually exists, always wrote the
                 # chat id here.
                 "channel_node": "'%s'" % name,
                 "channel": "has(hop.chat_id) ? hop.chat_id : ''",
                 "assistant": "has(context.assistant) && context.assistant != '' "
                              "? context.assistant : (has(hop.addressed_to) && "
                              "hop.addressed_to != '' ? hop.addressed_to : '%s')" % agent,
                 "chat_id": "has(hop.chat_id) ? hop.chat_id : ''",
                 "user_id": "has(hop.user_id) ? hop.user_id : ''",
                 "audience_set": "'[\"agent:%s\",\"member:%s\"]'" % (agent, person)}}},
        {"from": place.down(name), "to": place.up(),
         "condition": "has(hop.error_code)",
         "modifier": {"set_hop": {"route": "'error'"}}},
        {"from": place.up(), "to": place.down(name),
         "condition": "has(hop.route) && hop.route == 'answer' && "
                      "has(context.channel_node) && "
                      "context.channel_node == '%s'" % name},
    ]


def _screen_level(place, name, _p):
    # A screen is a channel too -- and it costs two edges, not three: what only
    # a screen produces is `event` and `receipt`, and an agent's ordinary
    # `answer` is the smallest view there is, so the down-edge RESTAMPS it.
    #
    # GH #522 -- both keys, and on a screen they carry the same word. A screen
    # IS one room, so its address and its conversation partner coincide; writing
    # the identity out anyway is what lets every holder downstream go on reading
    # `channel` and every answer go on routing by `channel_node`, whichever kind
    # of channel it came from.
    return [
        {"from": place.down(name), "to": place.up(),
         "condition": "has(hop.route) && (hop.route == 'event' || hop.route == 'receipt')",
         "modifier": {"set_context": {"channel_node": "'%s'" % name,
                                      "channel": "'%s'" % name}}},
        {"from": place.up(), "to": place.down(name),
         "condition": "has(hop.route) && (hop.route == 'answer' || hop.route == 'view') "
                      "&& has(context.channel_node) "
                      "&& context.channel_node == '%s'" % name,
         "modifier": {"set_hop": {"route": "'in_view'"}}},
    ]


def _app_level(place, name, p):
    # An app writes onto ONE screen, and what comes back is addressed by the
    # OWNER the display stamped -- the path of the cell that put the view up,
    # never anything the body claims. `hop.owner` is an ABSOLUTE path, so the
    # container stays in the guard whatever the declaration's scope is.
    return [
        {"from": place.down(name), "to": place.up(),
         "condition": "has(hop.route) && (hop.route == 'view' || hop.route == 'error')",
         "modifier": {"set_context": {"channel_node": "'%s'" % p["screen"],
                                      "channel": "'%s'" % p["screen"]}}},
        {"from": place.up(), "to": place.down(name),
         "condition": "has(hop.route) && (hop.route == 'event' || hop.route == 'receipt') "
                      "&& has(hop.owner) && hop.owner.contains('/%s/%s/')"
                      % (place.container, name)},
    ]


# level -> (container it is instantiated into, renderer, extra required params).
# The container is part of the table rather than a parameter: a member does not
# stand in `./people` in one colony and `./members` in another, and a level that
# could be told where it lives would stop being a level. Since GH #503 it is
# also the level's SCOPE, which is the same statement read as an address.
LEVELS = {
    "org":       ("orgs",       _container_level, []),
    "member":    ("members",    _container_level, []),
    "assistant": ("assistants", _assistant_level, []),
    "channel":   ("channels",   _channel_level,   ["assistant"]),
    "screen":    ("channels",   _screen_level,    []),
    "app":       ("apps",       _app_level,       ["screen"]),
}


def grow_level(p):
    level = p["level"]
    container, render, _extra = LEVELS[level]
    # The narrow form for every level, and the one exception is a reachability
    # fact rather than a taste: an identity door reaches the container's
    # sibling, which no declaration standing in the container can name. It is
    # written out at the branch that draws it, in `_assistant_level`.
    place = Place(container, not (level == "assistant" and p.get("subscribe")))
    node = {"name": place.node(p["name"]), "template": p["template"]}
    if isinstance(p.get("override_params"), dict):
        node["override_params"] = p["override_params"]
    # The birth state travels TOP-LEVEL on the entry, beside `template` and not
    # inside `override_params`: it is a property of the placement and not of a
    # cell's own settings, it covers the whole subtree the node brings, and the
    # door reads it exactly there (GH #472).
    birth = p.get("birth") or LEVEL_BIRTH.get(level)
    if birth:
        node["birth"] = birth
    # ONE declaration, not two: the node and its edges are one decision, and a
    # manifest rolls forward with no rollback -- a node that landed without its
    # edges is an island, which is the failure this recipe exists to prevent.
    ctx = p.get("ctx") if isinstance(p.get("ctx"), dict) else {}
    return [{"scope": place.scope(p["scope"]), "ctx": ctx,
             "diff": {"add_nodes": [node],
                      "add_edges": render(place, p["name"], p)}}]


RENDER = {"rewire_edge": rewire_edge, "add_node": add_node,
          "attach_drain": attach_drain, "grow_level": grow_level}

doc = json.load(sys.stdin)
msgs = doc["body"].get("messages") or []
payload = {}
for m in msgs:
    if m.get("text"):
        try:
            payload = json.loads(m["text"])
        except Exception:
            payload = {}

recipe = payload.get("recipe")
if recipe not in RENDER:
    # Cannot happen after `classify` -- and it is here anyway, because a cell
    # knows no topology and must not build on who stands in front of it.
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps({
        "header": {"operation": "recipe", "error_code": "recipe_unknown"},
        "messages": [{"origin": "tool", "type": "tool_result", "id": "",
                      "text": json.dumps({"reason": "no renderer for %r" % recipe})}]}))
    sys.exit(0)

params = payload.get("params") or {}
if recipe == "grow_level" and params.get("level") not in LEVELS:
    # Named, never guessed at. A level the table does not carry is a level whose
    # edge set nobody has written down, and rendering "something close" would
    # produce a subtree that boots and answers nothing.
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps({
        "header": {"operation": "recipe", "error_code": "level_unknown",
                   "recipe": recipe},
        "messages": [{"origin": "tool", "type": "tool_result", "id": "",
                      "text": json.dumps({"reason": "no level by that name",
                                          "level": str(params.get("level")),
                                          "known": sorted(LEVELS)})}]}))
    sys.exit(0)
if recipe == "grow_level" and params.get("birth") \
        and params.get("birth") not in BIRTH_STATES:
    # Named, never guessed at -- the same rule the level name follows. The door
    # refuses an unknown birth state pre-destructively, so nothing would be lost
    # by passing it through; what would be lost is the NAME of the refusal, one
    # hop away from the wish that made it.
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps({
        "header": {"operation": "recipe", "error_code": "birth_unknown",
                   "recipe": recipe},
        "messages": [{"origin": "tool", "type": "tool_result", "id": "",
                      "text": json.dumps({"reason": "no birth state by that name",
                                          "birth": str(params.get("birth")),
                                          "known": sorted(BIRTH_STATES)})}]}))
    sys.exit(0)
try:
    decls = RENDER[recipe](params)
except WishIncomplete as w:
    # GH #517 -- the wish did not say, so the recipe ASKS. It wears the code the
    # design lane already uses for exactly this act (`normalise`, a composer
    # that answers with a question instead of inventing a model id), because
    # the two are the same event on two lanes: a build that stopped because it
    # was not told enough, with the missing thing named in words a human can
    # answer.
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps({
        "header": {"operation": "recipe", "error_code": "wish_incomplete",
                   "recipe": recipe},
        "messages": [{"origin": "tool", "type": "tool_result", "id": "",
                      "text": json.dumps({"reason": w.question,
                                          "missing": ["ctx.%s" % w.key]})}]}))
    sys.exit(0)
except KeyError as e:
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps({
        "header": {"operation": "recipe", "error_code": "recipe_params_incomplete",
                   "recipe": recipe},
        "messages": [{"origin": "tool", "type": "tool_result", "id": "",
                      "text": json.dumps({"reason": "missing parameter %s" % e})}]}))
    sys.exit(0)

sha = digest(decls)
out = [{
    "header": {"operation": "recipe", "manifest_class": "fast",
               "manifest_sha256": sha, "declaration_count": len(decls)},
    "manifest": decls,
    "messages": [{"origin": "tool", "type": "tool_result", "id": "",
                  "text": "%s: %d declaration(s), scope %s" % (
                      recipe, len(decls), params.get("scope", "?"))}]}]

# GH #480 -- the fast lane writes down what a refusal will need, and it is the
# same two rows the design lane already writes.
#
# A refused submission comes back on `in_receipt`, which arrives on a FOREIGN
# chain by construction: `templates/submit/gate` renders the receipt off its own
# remembered row, so nothing of this build's context survives the round trip.
# `weave` recovers a composed build from two rows -- `normalise`'s digest
# binding, which says who owns those bytes, and the caller row, which says which
# door the answer goes to. A recipe wrote neither, so a refused fast-lane build
# ended as `build_unknown` and was delivered into `./orgs` rather than to the
# operator that asked (measured: `template_missing`, GH #480).
#
# The build id IS the digest. A fast-lane build has no other identity -- no
# composer opened a round to mint one -- and the digest is the one handle that
# survives the submitter's chain, because the submitter parks and pops a
# submission under it.
#
# `build_lane` is the third thing the row says, and it is the reason the row can
# be read at all: a model-free build has no composer, no thread and no question,
# so its refusal must NOT enter the repair machine. `weave` reads the marker off
# this row and takes the short road instead -- name the code, answer the door.
#
# Nothing is written for a REFUSED recipe: a build that produced no bytes has no
# digest to be refused under, and a row nobody can reach is a slate that only
# grows. And nothing is written when the context names NO caller at all -- the
# same guard `weave` parks its own row under (`names_a_caller`). There is no door
# to recover then, because none was ever stamped, and a slate written for a build
# nobody is waiting on is a table that only grows.
ctx = ((doc.get("envelope") or {}).get("header") or {}).get("context") or {}
caller = {k: str(ctx.get(k) or "") for k in CALLER_KEYS}
names_a_caller = any(caller.values())
caller["build_lane"] = "recipe"
now = datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%fZ")


def parked(slot, role, turn):
    return {"origin": "assistant", "type": "tool_call", "id": slot,
            "text": json.dumps({
                "operation": "insert", "table": "thread",
                "row": {"build_id": sha, "iter": 0, "role": role, "turn": turn,
                        "fired": 0, "recorded_at": now}})}


# `operation` is `bind` and not `recipe`: BOTH `./recipes -> .` edges match on
# `hop.operation == 'recipe'`, so a binding wearing that operation would leave
# the hive as a second answer to the same wish.
if names_a_caller:
    out.append({
        "header": {"route": "bind", "operation": "bind", "manifest_sha256": sha},
        "messages": [parked("w-fast-caller", "caller", json.dumps(caller)),
                     parked("w-fast-bind", "manifest", sha)]})
sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(out))

description.purpose: The fast lane: four predefined recipes rendered straight from their parameters into a manifest, with its sha256 digest. No model, no network, no disk -- what leaves here is a string built out of a dict. The fourth is grow_level, which renders the transit edge set a composition level gives a new child: it is the same set every time, so it is a table here rather than a paragraph a model rewrites per build. The counts live in the README, once, and a test derives them from this renderer. Two things ride BESIDE that set: a `birth` state written top-level on the node -- the door's own vocabulary, and a channel is rendered `inactive` because a connector opens its upstream the moment it has a task -- and, for an assistant and only when the wish asks, the identity door: the push edge from the member's own affinity record plus the receipt drain beside it.
description.use_when: Behind `classify` on hop.route == 'recipe', when the caller named a recipe and its parameters are complete.
description.not_in_scope: No inference, no retrieval, no application. No template CHOICE either: grow_level renders edges and is told which template to instantiate, because what a level should be filled with is a catalogue question and the catalogue is the librarian's. No subscription ROW either: writing one is a store write and not a mutation declaration, so it stays a `subscribe` op through affinity's own gate -- what is rendered here is the graph that row will need. And no rollback to lean on: the order of the declarations is semantics, because a manifest rolls forward and stops at the first refusal. And no ROUND to invent: the audience a grown channel's turns are spoken in is read off the wish's own `ctx` (`member_person`) and a wish that does not name it is asked, because a round is provenance and a wrong one blanks the whole memory behind a gate that is working exactly as specified (GH #517).
